ITV Regions: SVG to TOPOJSON¶

Taken from official ITV regional advertising webpage:

https://www.itvmedia.co.uk/get-started/regional-advertising

SVG image extracted from interactive map:

https://www-itvmedia-co-uk.filesusr.com/html/aca4fb_9bad0f91f0cdfc9f0ef135bedce2d7d2.html

Parse SVG¶

In [1]:
from IPython.display import SVG, display
from lxml import etree

# 1. Parse using recovery mode
parser = etree.XMLParser(recover=True)
tree = etree.parse("itv_regions.svg", parser)

# 2. Convert the recovered XML tree back to raw text bytes
clean_svg_bytes = etree.tostring(tree)

# 3. Display directly in your notebook
display(SVG(clean_svg_bytes))
In [2]:
from lxml import etree
from svgpathtools import parse_path
from shapely.geometry import Polygon
import geopandas as gpd

svg_file = "itv_regions.svg"

tree = etree.parse(svg_file)
root = tree.getroot()

def tag_name(el):
    return etree.QName(el).localname

regions = []
skipped = []

for anchor in root.iter():
    if tag_name(anchor) != "a":
        continue

    region_id = anchor.get("id")
    if not region_id:
        continue

    for path_el in anchor.iter():
        if tag_name(path_el) != "path":
            continue

        d = path_el.get("d")
        if not d:
            continue

        try:
            path = parse_path(d)

            # Split disconnected subpaths into continuous segments.
            subpaths = path.continuous_subpaths()

            for subpath in subpaths:
                if len(subpath) == 0:
                    continue

                # Only closed subpaths form polygon rings.
                if abs(subpath.start - subpath.end) > 1e-6:
                    skipped.append((region_id, "open subpath"))
                    continue

                points = [
                    (
                        subpath.point(i / 500).real,
                        subpath.point(i / 500).imag
                    )
                    for i in range(500)
                ]

                polygon = Polygon(points)

                if polygon.is_empty or polygon.area == 0:
                    continue

                if not polygon.is_valid:
                    polygon = polygon.buffer(0)

                if not polygon.is_empty:
                    regions.append({
                        "region": region_id,
                        "geometry": polygon
                    })

        except Exception as e:
            skipped.append((region_id, str(e)))

gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(regions, geometry="geometry")

print("Extracted polygons:", len(gdf))
print("\nPolygons per region:")
print(gdf.groupby("region").size())

print("\nSkipped paths/subpaths:", len(skipped))
print(skipped[:20])

gdf.to_file("itv_svg_polygons.geojson", driver="GeoJSON")

import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Keep the four UK countries and all relevant Channel Islands
wanted = [
    "England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland",
    "Jersey", "Guernsey", "Alderney", "Sark", "Herm"
]

reference = world[world["SUBUNIT"].isin(wanted)].copy()

# Project to British National Grid
reference = reference.to_crs("EPSG:27700")

# Split multipart geometries so individual island components can be removed
parts = reference.explode(index_parts=False).copy()
parts["cx"] = parts.geometry.centroid.x
parts["cy"] = parts.geometry.centroid.y

# Remove Orkney and Shetland components from Scotland
is_orkney_shetland = (
    parts["SUBUNIT"].eq("Scotland")
    & (parts["cy"] > 950_000)
    & (parts["cx"] < 500_000)
)

uk_reference = parts.loc[~is_orkney_shetland].copy()

# Check which reference regions remain
print(uk_reference["SUBUNIT"].value_counts())

# Plot the geographic reference
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 10))
uk_reference.plot(
    ax=ax,
    facecolor="whitesmoke",
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=0.6
)
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_title("UK and Channel Islands reference")
plt.show()

Manual Alignment - Whole of UK¶

In [8]:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import ipywidgets as widgets

from IPython.display import display, clear_output
from shapely.affinity import affine_transform

# Original SVG dimensions
SVG_WIDTH = 584
SVG_HEIGHT = 911

# Centre of the original SVG coordinate system
src_cx = SVG_WIDTH / 2
src_cy = SVG_HEIGHT / 2

# Centre and bounds of the geographic reference
minx, miny, maxx, maxy = uk_reference.total_bounds
target_cx = (minx + maxx) / 2
target_cy = (miny + maxy) / 2

# Initial scale: metres per SVG unit
initial_sx = (maxx - minx) / SVG_WIDTH
initial_sy = (maxy - miny) / SVG_HEIGHT

# Controls
scale_x = widgets.FloatSlider(
    value=initial_sx, min=500, max=3000, step=10,
    description="Width", readout_format=".0f",
    continuous_update=False
)

scale_y = widgets.FloatSlider(
    value=initial_sy, min=500, max=3000, step=10,
    description="Height", readout_format=".0f",
    continuous_update=False
)

rotation = widgets.FloatSlider(
    value=0, min=-20, max=20, step=0.5,
    description="Rotation (°)", continuous_update=False
)

shift_x = widgets.FloatSlider(
    value=0, min=-300000, max=300000, step=5000,
    description="Move X (km)", continuous_update=False
)

shift_y = widgets.FloatSlider(
    value=0, min=-300000, max=300000, step=5000,
    description="Move Y (km)", continuous_update=False
)

opacity = widgets.FloatSlider(
    value=0.45, min=0.1, max=1, step=0.05,
    description="Opacity", continuous_update=False
)

output = widgets.Output()

def transform_geometry(geom, sx, sy, angle, dx, dy):
    """Scale, flip SVG Y, rotate and position a polygon."""
    theta = np.radians(angle)
    c, s = np.cos(theta), np.sin(theta)

    # SVG Y increases downwards, unlike geographic Y
    a = c * sx
    b = s * sy
    d = s * sx
    e = -c * sy

    xoff = target_cx + dx - a * src_cx - b * src_cy
    yoff = target_cy + dy - d * src_cx - e * src_cy

    return affine_transform(
        geom, [a, b, d, e, xoff, yoff]
    )

def redraw(*args):
    with output:
        clear_output(wait=True)

        aligned = gdf.copy()
        aligned["geometry"] = aligned.geometry.apply(
            lambda geom: transform_geometry(
                geom,
                scale_x.value,
                scale_y.value,
                rotation.value,
                shift_x.value,
                shift_y.value
            )
        )

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 10))

        # Real-world geographic outline
        uk_reference.plot(
            ax=ax,
            facecolor="whitesmoke",
            edgecolor="black",
            linewidth=0.7
        )

        # Transformed ITV SVG polygons
        aligned.plot(
            ax=ax,
            column="region",
            alpha=opacity.value,
            edgecolor="red",
            linewidth=0.5,
            legend=False
        )

        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.set_title("ITV SVG alignment")
        ax.set_axis_off()
        plt.show()

        # Keep the latest transformed polygons available
        globals()["gdf_aligned"] = aligned

for control in [
    scale_x, scale_y, rotation, shift_x, shift_y, opacity
]:
    control.observe(redraw, names="value")

display(
    widgets.VBox([
        scale_x, scale_y, rotation,
        shift_x, shift_y, opacity
    ]),
    output
)

redraw()

Manual Alignement - NI & Channel Islands¶

In [ ]:
import ipywidgets as widgets
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, clear_output
from shapely.affinity import affine_transform
import numpy as np

# Split the two groups out of the original SVG polygons
ni = gdf[gdf["region"] == "ulster"].copy()
ci = gdf[gdf["region"] == "channelIslands"].copy()

# Reference geography for each group
ni_ref = uk_reference[uk_reference["SUBUNIT"] == "Northern Ireland"]
ci_ref = uk_reference[
    uk_reference["SUBUNIT"].isin(
        ["Jersey", "Guernsey", "Alderney", "Sark", "Herm"]
    )
]

# Use the saved Great Britain transformation as the starting point
base = {
    "sx": scale_x.value,
    "sy": scale_y.value,
    "angle": rotation.value,
    "dx": shift_x.value,
    "dy": shift_y.value,
}

def make_controls(prefix):
    return {
        "sx": widgets.FloatSlider(
            value=base["sx"], min=500, max=3000, step=10,
            description=f"{prefix} width", continuous_update=False
        ),
        "sy": widgets.FloatSlider(
            value=base["sy"], min=500, max=3000, step=10,
            description=f"{prefix} height", continuous_update=False
        ),
        "angle": widgets.FloatSlider(
            value=0, min=-20, max=20, step=0.5,
            description=f"{prefix} rotation", continuous_update=False
        ),
        "dx": widgets.FloatSlider(
            value=0, min=-500000, max=500000, step=5000,
            description=f"{prefix} move X", continuous_update=False
        ),
        "dy": widgets.FloatSlider(
            value=0, min=-500000, max=500000, step=5000,
            description=f"{prefix} move Y", continuous_update=False
        ),
    }

ni_controls = make_controls("NI")
ci_controls = make_controls("CI")

def apply_group_transform(frame, controls):
    aligned = frame.copy()
    aligned["geometry"] = aligned.geometry.apply(
        lambda geom: transform_geometry(
            geom,
            controls["sx"].value,
            controls["sy"].value,
            controls["angle"].value,
            base["dx"] + controls["dx"].value,
            base["dy"] + controls["dy"].value
        )
    )
    return aligned

# Note: transform_geometry uses the SVG centre and geographic reference
# centre. The offset sliders here are additional adjustments to that baseline.
island_output = widgets.Output()

def redraw_islands(*args):
    with island_output:
        clear_output(wait=True)

        ni_aligned = apply_group_transform(ni, ni_controls)
        ci_aligned = apply_group_transform(ci, ci_controls)

        # Combine the saved Great Britain polygons with the adjusted groups
        combined = __import__("pandas").concat(
            [gdf_gb_aligned, ni_aligned, ci_aligned],
            ignore_index=True
        )
        globals()["gdf_aligned"] = combined

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 10))

        uk_reference.plot(
            ax=ax, facecolor="whitesmoke",
            edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.7
        )

        gdf_gb_aligned.plot(
            ax=ax, color="steelblue",
            alpha=0.45, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.4
        )
        ni_aligned.plot(
            ax=ax, color="orange",
            alpha=0.65, edgecolor="red", linewidth=0.6
        )
        ci_aligned.plot(
            ax=ax, color="green",
            alpha=0.65, edgecolor="red", linewidth=0.6
        )

        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.set_title("Adjust Northern Ireland and Channel Islands")
        ax.set_axis_off()
        plt.show()

for controls in [ni_controls, ci_controls]:
    for slider in controls.values():
        slider.observe(redraw_islands, names="value")

display(widgets.HTML("<b>Northern Ireland</b>"))
display(widgets.VBox(list(ni_controls.values())))
display(widgets.HTML("<b>Channel Islands</b>"))
display(widgets.VBox(list(ci_controls.values())))
display(island_output)

redraw_islands()

import geopandas as gpd

# Ensure geometries are valid
gdf_export = gdf_aligned.copy()
gdf_export = gdf_export[
    gdf_export.geometry.notna() & ~gdf_export.geometry.is_empty
].copy()

# Check and repair invalid geometries if necessary
invalid_count = (~gdf_export.geometry.is_valid).sum()
print("Invalid geometries before repair:", invalid_count)

if invalid_count:
    gdf_export["geometry"] = gdf_export.geometry.make_valid()

# Use WGS84 longitude/latitude for GeoJSON
gdf_export = gdf_export.set_crs("EPSG:27700", allow_override=True)
gdf_export = gdf_export.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

# Keep only useful attributes
gdf_export = gdf_export[["region", "geometry"]]

# Save
gdf_export.to_file(
    "itv_regions_aligned.geojson",
    driver="GeoJSON"
)

print("Saved itv_regions_aligned.geojson")
print("Polygons:", len(gdf_export))
print("Regions:", sorted(gdf_export["region"].unique()))

import geopandas as gpd
import topojson as tp

# Combine all polygon pieces belonging to each ITV region
gdf_regions = gdf_export.dissolve(by="region", as_index=False)

print("Regions:", len(gdf_regions))
print(gdf_regions["region"].tolist())

# Convert to TopoJSON
topology = tp.Topology(
    gdf_regions,
    object_name="itv_regions",
    prequantize=True
)

topology.to_json("itv_regions_aligned.topojson")

print("Saved itv_regions_aligned.topojson")
